content: Metoprolol tartrate tablets are prescribed for the treatment of hypertension, angina pectoris, and myocardial infarction, including both early and late phases of management. Below are detailed instructions for its administration: Hypertension The dosage of metoprolol tartrate tablets must be tailored to the individual patient. These tablets should be taken with or immediately following meals. The typical starting dose is 100 mg daily, which can be administered as a single dose or divided into two doses. This dosage can be used alone or in combination with a diuretic. Dosage adjustments may be made at weekly or longer intervals until optimal blood pressure control is achieved. The maximum effect of any given dose is generally observed after one week of therapy. The effective dosage range is between 100 mg and 450 mg per day. Dosages exceeding 450 mg per day have not been studied. While once-daily dosing is effective in maintaining blood pressure reduction throughout the day, lower doses (e.g., 100 mg) may not sustain full efficacy at the end of the 24-hour period. In such cases, higher or more frequent daily doses may be necessary. Blood pressure should be measured near the end of the dosing interval to ensure adequate control throughout the day. It is important to note that beta-1 selectivity diminishes as the dose of metoprolol increases. Angina Pectoris The dosage of metoprolol tartrate tablets should also be individualized for patients with angina. These tablets should be taken with or immediately following meals. The usual initial dose is 100 mg daily, divided into two doses. Dosage may be gradually increased at weekly intervals until the desired clinical response is achieved or until significant slowing of the heart rate occurs. The effective dosage range for angina is 100 mg to 400 mg per day. Dosages above 400 mg per day have not been studied. If treatment is to be discontinued, the dosage should be reduced gradually over a period of 1 to 2 weeks to avoid adverse effects. Myocardial Infarction Early Treatment In the acute phase of a confirmed or suspected myocardial infarction, metoprolol tartrate treatment should be initiated as soon as possible after the patient’s arrival at the hospital. Treatment should begin in a coronary care or similar unit once the patient’s hemodynamic condition has stabilized. The initial treatment involves intravenous administration of three bolus injections of 5 mg metoprolol tartrate, given at approximately 2-minute intervals. During intravenous administration, blood pressure, heart rate, and electrocardiogram (ECG) should be closely monitored. Patients who tolerate the full intravenous dose (15 mg) should begin oral metoprolol tartrate tablets at a dose of 50 mg every 6 hours, starting 15 minutes after the last intravenous dose. This regimen should continue for 48 hours. After the initial 48 hours, patients should transition to a maintenance dose of 100 mg twice daily. Patients who do not tolerate the full intravenous dose should start with oral metoprolol tartrate tablets at 25 mg or 50 mg every 6 hours, depending on their level of tolerance, beginning 15 minutes after the last intravenous dose or as soon as their clinical condition permits. In cases of severe intolerance, metoprolol treatment should be discontinued. Late Treatment Patients who have contraindications to early treatment, those who do not tolerate the full early treatment, or those for whom therapy is delayed for any reason should begin metoprolol tartrate tablets at a dose of 100 mg twice daily as soon as their clinical condition allows. Therapy should be continued for at least 3 months. Although the efficacy of metoprolol beyond 3 months has not been definitively established, data from studies with other beta-blockers suggest that treatment should be continued for 1 to 3 years. These instructions are adapted from the FDA package insert for metoprolol tartrate.
